newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Quiet Russian MinFins ease as H1 profits taken.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Russian MinFins ease as H1 profits taken.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds eased in calm trading on Thursday as the market eyed the future of U.S. interest rates, with traders taking profits to close half-year books.

"Although people are not expecting a U.S. rate hike, the possibility of one is making them nervous," a Sberbank dealer said. "Profit-taking has been seen all over the emerging market, given the decline in U.S. Treasuries."
The next U.S. Federal Open Market Committee policy-making meeting is due on July 1 and July 2.
MinFins, like other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said the day's was slow, with banks squaring positions at the end of the half year amid a seasonal decline in activity.
But one dealer said some buying interest was seen for the sixth and seventh tranches, while other papers fluctuated in mixed trading.
